Title: March 5, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: Flock Safety Cameras
Topic1.Summary: Multiple residents urged council to cancel or not renew the Flock Safety license-plate-reader contract, citing immigration enforcement concerns, data-sharing risks, security vulnerabilities, and Flock's alleged misconduct. Speakers asked for public votes and data-retention policies, and some pointed to Denver, Longmont, and state legislation as examples. Council members said they were uncomfortable with the vulnerabilities and that staff is developing both near-term contract decisions and a broader policy. Staff noted that policy on surveillance and data sharing falls within council's purview.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment: South Boulder Recreation Center
Topic2.Summary: Many speakers, including seniors, swimmers, parents, and a 10-year-old student, urged council to keep the South Boulder Rec Center open with its pool, gym, and basketball court. Speakers cited crowded pools, the loss of other city pools, walkability, and the 15-minute neighborhood goal. Staff said a study session on facilities funding is scheduled for April 9 that will cover rec centers.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Item 3E Area Three Guidance
Topic3.Summary: Council pulled item 3E, the Area Three planning reserve resolution, for separate discussion. Council members agreed to revise the language so Area Three housing is not limited to middle-income ownership and can include other housing types such as senior or service-supported housing. Council gave a unanimous straw poll direction to staff, and the remaining consent agenda items were approved unanimously.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up Check-In: 3550 and 3850 Frontier Avenue Redevelopment
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for a mixed-use redevelopment with a 2,500-capacity events venue, a hotel, about 500 apartments, and commercial space, requiring rezoning and height modifications. Council members said they did not need to call up the project and were open to legislative action if needed to allow it. Staff noted that a tailored zone district may be needed and that council would review specific issues such as inclusionary housing at site review.

Topic5.Title: 2026 Board and Commission Appointments
Topic5.Summary: Council held a public hearing on 2026 board and commission appointments, with two speakers offering general comments. The city clerk explained the nomination and voting process, and council nominated and voted on candidates for each open seat, including the Boulder Urban Renewal Authority. Council unanimously approved the 2026 appointments, with the Urban Renewal Authority appointments taking effect immediately.

Topic6.Title: Affordable Housing Review
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented an overview of Boulder's affordable housing program, including the gap between incomes and home prices, the rental and ownership market, supply and demand programs, and partnerships with Boulder Housing Partners. Staff said the city has produced affordable units at about 37 percent of new development, outperforming its 25 percent inclusionary requirement, and that most local funding comes from local sources. Council asked about middle-income ownership, cash-in-lieu payments, the 15 percent housing goal, unused down-payment funds, and land banking, and staff said next steps include zoning reforms, expanded down-payment assistance, and continued innovation.
